quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2026 results: sales were $4.7 billion, growing 22% reported and 15% organically year over year, with growth in both segments and both above guidance. Record adjusted EPS of $2.72 (up 33% year over year; GAAP EPS $2.53) and record adjusted operating income of over $1 billion at a 22.2% adjusted operating margin, up 180 basis points. Cash from operations was $865 million and free cash flow $608 million, with roughly 100% returned to shareholders through buybacks and dividends. CEO Terrence Curtin: 'We delivered over 20% sales growth in the first quarter with growth in both segments by driving content growth above market.'
quarterly_data.figure: sales $4.7 billion (+22% reported, +15% organic); adjusted EPS $2.72 (+33%); adjusted operating margin 22.2% (+180 basis points); free cash flow $608 million

quarterly_data.signal: Record orders: orders rose by over $1 billion year over year to $5.1 billion with a book-to-bill of 1.1, and double-digit organic order growth in all regions. Industrial segment orders grew over 40% with essentially every business up double digits (momentum in digital data networks, energy and AD&M); Transportation orders increased 11% and grew in all businesses. CEO: 'The DDN orders were up 70% year-over-year in the quarter', and 'if you exclude the DDN orders, our orders were up double digit across TE.' Some AI orders are for programs further out, so part of the order book lands later in the year.
quarterly_data.figure: orders $5.1 billion (record, up over $1 billion); book-to-bill 1.1; Industrial orders up over 40%; Transportation orders up 11%; DDN orders up 70% year-over-year

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q2 2026 guidance: sales of $4.7 billion, up 13% reported and 6% organically year over year, with adjusted EPS around $2.65 (20% growth). Industrial Solutions is expected to grow sequentially (up double digits), partly offset by auto seasonality - global auto production down about 3 million units from Q1 to Q2 (versus about 2 million in an average year) within an unchanged fiscal 2026 view of roughly 88 million units. The Q1-to-Q2 EPS bridge is mainly $0.04 or $0.05 of higher tax and interest expense. Management expects fiscal 2026 growth ahead of the long-term through-cycle target of 6 to 8 points of annual average growth, with both segments at 30% plus incremental flow-through.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 FY2026 sales $4.7 billion (+13% reported, +6% organic); adjusted EPS around $2.65 (+20%); auto production down about 3 million units Q1 to Q2; FY2026 growth ahead of the 6 to 8 points target

quarterly_data.signal: AI connectivity outlook raised: Digital Data Networks grew 70% year over year and AI revenue was higher than expected. 'We now expect our AI revenues in fiscal 2026 to be a couple of hundred million dollars higher than our view 90 days ago, with growth expected across every hyperscale customer.' Against the Investor Day goal of 'a $3 billion of AI revenue out a couple of years', Curtin said 'we're certainly on track to achieve this' and that this year's number 'will be $200 million more than what we just shared', with the bulk of the increase coming in Q3 and Q4 as programs ramp and into 2027. TE is increasing investment in the DDN business to support the acceleration.
quarterly_data.figure: DDN sales grew 70% year-over-year; FY2026 AI revenue $200 million more than the view 90 days ago; $3 billion AI revenue target on track

quarterly_data.signal: How the AI ramp is built: the growth is new program awards with hyperscalers - 'we aren't going to talk at the customer level', but 'these are hyperscaler programs' and the content spans 'across power and data and signal' as customers move to next-generation architectures. 'Some of the awards we got in the first quarter are for later this year into 2027', and 'those programs will ramp here over the next couple of quarters and really be bigger in quarter 3 and quarter 4 than what's happening now.' 'It is a mix of some programs continuing to ramp, but also new programs with the customers that will ramp in the second half.' 'We grew AI programs from quarter 4 to quarter 1 sequentially', and asked by an analyst whether the raised AI outlook was held back by capacity, Curtin said: 'I don't think it has anything to do with capacity constraints.'

Capex raised for AI program wins: 'we are increasing our capital expenditure this year to support the growth -- growing pipeline of customer awards for AI programs. We now expect CapEx to be closer to 6% of our sales this year', while still expecting at least 100% free cash flow conversion for fiscal 2026. CFO Heath Mitts said the spend is tied to specific program wins with aggressive ramp windows over the next couple of quarters to support production in the second half and into fiscal 2027: 'there is a specific tooling involved and most of that's going into existing production facilities that we have throughout Asia and a little bit in North America', adding 'we would not be spending that money if we didn't have revenue and profits tied to it.'
quarterly_data.figure: CapEx closer to 6% of our sales this year; at least 100% free cash flow conversion

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain for the AI ramps is not the constraint: 'we are able to procure what we need to procure.' Hyperscalers give longer-dated orders because ramps are very fast - 'they're reserving capacity for the programs' and 'These are not generic components that we're making here.' The pressure is metals: 'There is inflation around things that are metal related', and per the CFO the metals category 'is our largest purchase category'; TE is passing it through via pricing ('that inflation is being passed through') and does not 'expect any significant time lapse' in recovery. On DRAM: 'We don't buy significant memory that impacts our supply chain' and 'the memory situation is not impacting us at all'. Elsewhere capacity is in a good spot, with additions in energy and aerospace.

Energy (grid/utility power connectivity): sales grew 88% including the Richards acquisition, and organically 15%, 'driven by continued increased investments by customers in grid hardening and renewable applications', with strong growth in both the United States and Europe. On momentum: 'It hasn't slowed down at all.' Management expects organic double-digit growth this year on top of the inorganic benefit, and 'Richards is doing very well to its original plan, but we're adding capacity there to expand for our energy business'.

Segment detail: Industrial Solutions sales grew 38% (26% organic) with adjusted operating margin expanding by over 500 basis points to 23% on volume leverage; within it automation and connected living grew 12% organically (factory automation recovering in all regions; residential HVAC and appliances still soft), AD&M 11% organically and medical 5% organically. Transportation Solutions grew 10% (7% organic) with adjusted operating margins above 21%; auto grew 7% organically with growth over market at the high end of the 4- to 6-point range (driven by China and Europe), commercial transportation grew 16% organically on Asia and Europe recovery, and sensors were essentially flat. Management expects global truck build up 200 basis points, with North America the wildcard.
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial Solutions +38% (26% organic), margin 23% (over 500 basis points expansion); Transportation +10% (7% organic), margin above 21%; commercial transportation 16%
